


Aiken (Harvard professor of math): "In the US, there was a need for 5 or 6 machines [like EDVAC], but no more."


Commercialization track:
1945: ENIAC (used for ballistics tables), is an entire room. created by Eckert and Mauchly
1948: E&M spin out of of university of ?, presell 20 UNIVAC computers for $1M ($11M today) each
    - several random customers for military and beaurocratic usage. There were clear tasks that could be automated! (also, the word "automate" was brought into fame by Ford co. in 1947)
    - EDSAC was a contract programming group, "scientific computing as a service"
    - this company dies/gets acquired in the 1950's..?
1952: IBM 701 mainframe. 
    - Main customer=LANL
    - computer rental: $20K/mo. ($170,000/mo today) or $1M outright (https://ed-thelen.org/comp-hist/BRL61-ibm07.html)
    - this suggests about 40 month timeline for operation; this is tight given how quickly computing tech improves!
    - 1954: IBM 704 introduces _core memory_: small, stable, and has random access (constant time retrieval!), not O(memory-size) access

1955: 2nd generation: nSA commissions Philco to make a transistor computer
 - IBM follows up with 7090, transisstor-based machine delievered around 1959
 - IBM 7094 rental: $30K per month ($330K/mo. today), or 1.6M outright purchase ($17M today)
 - IBM stretch 1960: $13.5M (later $6.7M) ($145M, later $72M) purchase price, invented lookahead, bytes,
